title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness and starvation/timeouts
author: Anjali Mehta
description: Summary: Tune the continuous-batcher scheduler to reduce request starvation, improve queueing fairness across classes (interactive vs batch), and tighten timeouts for KV cache warmups. Motivation: we've seen intermittent p99 latency regressions and starvation alerts in multi-tenant workloads where low-priority long-running batches could block interactive requests during load spikes. This PR adjusts scheduling credits, introduces age-based priority bumping, implements per-request max-queue-time and starvation thresholds, and improves timeout handling for KV-cache-backed requests. Key changes: 1) Scheduler policy: add fairness_credit accounting (leaky-bucket style) so each priority class receives proportional dequeue opportunities; introduce age-based priority bumping to prevent long-tail starvation; bound preemption to avoid thrashing. 2) Timeouts: add configurable max_queue_time_ms and starvation_threshold_ms; requests that exceed max_queue_time are fast-failed with structured error for caller backoff; requests that hit starvation_threshold are promoted one level to ensure eventual progress. 3) KV cache integration: add warmup-aware timeouts so requests waiting on KV-cache hits have separate, slightly relaxed queue timeouts and metrics tagging so we can distinguish cache-wait-induced latency. 4) Observability: new metrics (batcher.queue_time_seconds_bucket, batcher.starvation_promotions_total, batcher.fairness_credits) and dashboards updated; trace spans include scheduler_decision tags. 5) Config surface: continuous_batcher/config.yaml adds sane defaults and per-deployment knobs for dedicated vs hosted profiles. Results: perf-canary and internal benchmarks show ~12% reduction in p99 latency for mixed interactive/batch workloads and 18% throughput improvement under high concurrency with no measurable regression in median latency. Starvation alerts in daily canaries went from 7/day to 0/day. Rollout plan: gated feature flag (scheduler.v2_fairness) enabled on perf-canary, then staged to dedicated clusters for 48h before global rollout. Backout: revert feature flag and config. Testing: unit tests for scheduler logic, integration tests for starvation promotion, perf canary runs included (perf-canary/continuous-batcher-scenario-2026-02-18). Related: ENG-1286 (scheduler fairness), ENG-1420 (kv-cache warmup timeouts).

review_comments: Carlos Rivera: Nice work — the fairness_credit model looks sound. Two asks: (1) add a short explanation in scheduler.rs about the rationale for the chosen decay constant, and (2) make the default starvation_threshold_ms conservative for hosted runs.
Anjali Mehta: Addressed both; added comments and bumped hosted default to 1200ms (was 800ms). Added note in CHANGELOG about default change.
Priya Singh: Question: could age-based promotions cause head-of-line blocking for high-priority short requests? Recommend we bound promotions per-window.
Anjali Mehta: Bound promotions to 1 per-request per-interval (configurable). Added tests to ensure no thrashing.
Ethan Zhao: CI flaked on batcher_evict_test; reran and passed on second run. Verified canary numbers are stable.
Carlos Rivera: Approving after test flake addressed and observed canary improvements.
